caption: One week after an Anthropic researcher's internal doomsday warning went public, CEO Dario Amodei laid out a formal framework for managing the pace of frontier AI development. The plan — which Amodei is calling 'pace the frontier' — relies on independent safety evaluators and coordination between AI labs operating in democratic countries. It has picked up some early industry support, but it has also drawn pointed resistance from Nvidia's Jensen Huang, making the Amodei-Huang split the most visible fault line in the AI governance debate right now. Source is TechCrunch's Equity podcast, hosted by Kirsten Korosec, Anthony Ha, and Sean O'Kane. The episode also covers Automattic's boardroom coup and several major deals, both of which the slides here skip. The real tension the Equity hosts surface — and the one this carousel leaves open — is whether competing labs can ever actually agree on what slowing down means, and who has the authority to enforce it. Where do you come down: industry self-governance, or mandatory regulatory oversight?
